claim: Public tagged send/receive wrappers dispatch through the endpoint operation tables, while context/tag/address/descriptor have separate roles.
Core fi_getinfo rejects newer requested API versions, iterates eligible provider callbacks, filters/reorders results, and returns ENODATA without a result.
Input mode bits advertise application obligations; returned required modes must be implemented, unlike service capability requirements.
Provider registration validates name, mandatory fabric entrypoint, supported interface version, type, and include/exclude filtering.
EFA provider builds direct information before protocol-based RDM entries where available, but caller requirements still determine compatibility.
EFA direct attribute tests exclude FI_TAGGED and FI_ATOMIC and distinguish direct progress/size/ordering attributes.
API 2.7 direct mode without FI_CONTEXT2 returns no context2 requirement and zero inject size; older requests have different eligibility.
Endpoint close can discard outstanding work without completions; buffers remain valid until completion or endpoint close returns.
Fabric children must be released before fabric close; endpoint bindings and scalable child contexts impose separate resource dependencies.
AV insertion returns local handles rather than globally meaningful ranks; lookup/removal has its own lifetime and representation.
EFA AV stores raw endpoint address, QPN/QKey, address handles and reverse lookup; RDM layers endpoint-specific peers above the base AV.
Direct AV test checks full address insertion/lookup and failure after removal, not a portable fixed handle value.
Tagged matching compares sender and receiver tags after receive ignore bits are masked out.
Directed receive functional tests explicitly select efa and parameterize operation, size, memory type and completion semantics.
RMA wrapper separates peer handle, remote address/key, local descriptor, and operation context.
Atomic validity is specific to write/fetch/compare operation family, datatype, operation, and element count.
EFA RMA read unit test conditionally expects EOPNOTSUPP or one mocked device request after valid local registration.
EFA manual documents no FI_RMA_EVENT and target AV insertion prerequisites for direct or homogeneous-peer RMA configurations.
MR_LOCAL, VIRT_ADDR, PROV_KEY, ENDPOINT, and HMEM govern different registration/address/key/lifetime responsibilities.
EFA MR validation rejects excess IOV count with EINVAL and an uninitialized CUDA interface with ENOSYS.
Cache-hit test registers one buffer twice, asserts shared cache-entry identity, closes both handles, then frees the allocation.
HMEM interface availability and P2P availability are distinct; P2P disabled CUDA test retains initialized interface but clears direct support.
EFA P2P policy validation distinguishes REQUIRED, PREFERRED, ENABLED, DISABLED and interface/API restrictions.
CQ read returns entries, EAGAIN when none, or EAVAIL requiring readerr; format determines which fields are available.
EFA RDM CQ progress can post initial internal receives, poll device queues and service endpoint protocol state.
Initial receive test verifies zero-count CQ read posts initial pool-sized internal receives and clears scan state.
Injected send failure expects EAVAIL and validates provider error translation through the CQ error path.
EFA domain stores variant identity/device/protection domain/MR pool; lock policy depends on negotiated threading obligations.
RDM endpoint owns packet pools, endpoint-specific peer maps, backoff and queued handshake/protocol work.
Generic send resolves peer and checks backoff, packet capacity, and TX operation pool before protocol posting.
Current send first tries refactored selector with ordered eager, medium, runtread, longread, longcts candidates before legacy fallback.
Eager eligibility subtracts actual request-header size from MTU; construction produces one packet with operation pointer/callback.
Longread requires P2P, every source IOV registered, interface size threshold, and peer RDMA-read interoperability.
Runtread adds delivery-complete exclusion, read-message-in-flight and positive peer runt allowance gates.
Selector releases temporary MRs before legacy fallback and forced protocol replaces normal size selection.
Eager device completion and delivery receipt use separate completion/release predicates.
Tagged incoming request path carries callbacks for matched and later unexpected-message matching.
Eager tests check successful TX retirement and exactly-once failed-post message-ID rollback/resource release.
Forced CUDA read functional test gates prerequisites, isolates control traffic, and validates device read counters.
